# EulerFactorZeros — one wheel's Euler factor, and why two wheels never share a zero

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [Survivor shares and analytic inputs](../../GRAPH.md#survivor-shares-and-analytic-inputs)

Each prime wheel has an Euler factor, one minus the prime to the power minus s. Its zeros are evenly spaced up the imaginary axis, one every 2π over the logarithm of the prime: the wheel's own period on the logarithmic scale. The periods of two different prime wheels never line up (no whole multiple of the logarithm of one prime equals a whole multiple of the logarithm of another, except zero), which is unique factorization, the same fact that makes the wheels independent in the Chinese Remainder Theorem. So the Euler factors of two different wheels share exactly one zero, at s = 0. This is the case of the rational numbers of Theorem 1.7.1.1 (1) and (3) in Masullo's preprint, where it is used to choose the topologies for his trace formula; it is a classical fact, not new here.

**What it adds:** CRT says the wheels are independent as remainders; this node gives the same independence on the analytic side, as the zeros of the wheels' Euler factors.

## Published sources

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [Fundamental theorem of arithmetic (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic) — unique factorization, which makes a power of one prime never a power of another
- [Euler product (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_product) — the Euler factors 1 - p^(-s) whose zeros this node describes
- A. M. Masullo, The Music of the Primes (preprint, 2026) — Theorem 1.7.1.1 (1) and (3) in the case of the rationals; this node proves that case

## Claims

<a id="euler_factor_zeros"></a>
### `euler_factor_zeros`

For a prime p, the Euler factor 1 - p^(-s) vanishes exactly at the whole multiples of 2πi / log p.

```lean
/-- **The zeros of one wheel's Euler factor.** For a prime `p`, the Euler
factor `1 - p^(-s)` vanishes exactly at the whole multiples of `2πi / log p`. -/
def euler_factor_zeros : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ s : ℂ,
    (1 : ℂ) - (p : ℂ) ^ (-s) = 0 ↔
      ∃ k : ℤ, s = (k : ℂ) * (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I) / (Real.log p : ℂ)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.EulerFactorZeros.euler_factor_zeros_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/EulerFactorZeros.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/EulerFactorZeros.lean)

<a id="log_periods_independent"></a>
### `log_periods_independent`

For different primes p and q, a whole multiple of log p equals a whole multiple of log q only when both multiples are zero.

```lean
/-- **The periods of two wheels never line up.** For different primes `p` and
`q`, a whole multiple `a` of `log p` equals a whole multiple `b` of `log q`
only when both multiples are zero. -/
def log_periods_independent : Prop :=
  ∀ p q : ℕ, p.Prime → q.Prime → p ≠ q → ∀ a b : ℤ,
    (a : ℝ) * Real.log p = (b : ℝ) * Real.log q → a = 0 ∧ b = 0
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.EulerFactorZeros.log_periods_independent_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/EulerFactorZeros.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/EulerFactorZeros.lean)

<a id="euler_factor_common_zero"></a>
### `euler_factor_common_zero`

For different primes p and q, the only common zero of 1 - p^(-s) and 1 - q^(-s) is s = 0.

```lean
/-- **Two wheels share one zero.** For different primes `p` and `q`, the only
common zero of the Euler factors `1 - p^(-s)` and `1 - q^(-s)` is `s = 0`. -/
def euler_factor_common_zero : Prop :=
  ∀ p q : ℕ, p.Prime → q.Prime → p ≠ q → ∀ s : ℂ,
    (1 : ℂ) - (p : ℂ) ^ (-s) = 0 → (1 : ℂ) - (q : ℂ) ^ (-s) = 0 → s = 0
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.EulerFactorZeros.euler_factor_common_zero_step` in [`RNSSolutions/EulerFactorZeros.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/EulerFactorZeros.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)
